title: cost-opt: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Automates and centralizes cost-optimization defaults and tooling for inference workloads. This PR implements: 1) Autotuned defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching that reduce per-token cost with minimal latency impact; 2) Quantization profile registry + automatic selection heuristics for common model families; 3) Unit-economics tooling: a CLI and server-side endpoints that compute per-route token cost, effective throughput, and suggested config diffs; 4) Console integration: new per-route recommendations and a small docs update. Motivation: teams repeatedly tune batching/caching/quant manually. We want a safe, opt-in autotune path that yields improved unit economics out-of-the-box and surface clear suggestions in the Console. Design highlights: - Autotune controller (runtime): collects short warm-up statistics (seq length distributions, concurrency) and computes target batch/window sizes and cache TTLs. Controller exposes conservative and aggressive profiles. - Quant profile registry: JSON-based profiles per model_family -> preferred quant format (int8, q4_0, q4_k_m), expected quality delta, and fallback options. Profiles are versioned and vendored in model-registry. - Unit-econ tooling: server endpoint /api/v1/uecon/simulate and a CLI `rw-uecon simulate` that accepts route usage traces and returns suggested config changes and estimated cost delta. - Safety: autotune only applies runtime defaults for new routes or routes explicitly marked `autotune: true`. All changes are logged, estimations are shown in Console, and there is a one-click rollback. Checklist: - [x] Runtime controller implementation with metrics export - [x] Quant profile registry + selection heuristic - [x] Unit-econ API + CLI - [x] Console UI: per-route recommendation card and simulation results link - [x] Tests: unit tests for heuristics, integration tests for controller behavior - [x] Docs: usage + migration notes - [x] Feature flag gated rollout and canary policy
Local testing: ran perf canary against a synthetic chat workload (seq length mean=120, p95=650) and saw median per-token cost reduction of ~18% under conservative profile, p95 latency impact <3% for low-concurrency routes. Commits (summary): - 1a2b3c4: runtime: add autotune controller, metrics, and config store integration - 2b3c4d5: runtime: apply batching & cache defaults on route creation + API for rollbacks - 3c4d5e6: model-registry: add quant profiles v1 and selection heuristic - 4d5e6f7: uecon: add simulation API and CLI client - 5e6f7g8: console: add recommendations card, simulation link + docs pages - 6f7g8h9: tests: integration and unit tests for autotune and uecon tooling Files changed (high level): - redwood/runtime/controller/* (autotune controller, heuristics, metrics) - redwood/runtime/config_store.go (apply/rollback logic) - redwood-model-registry/profiles/quant-profiles.json (new file) - redwood-model-registry/selection/heuristic.go - redwood/uecon/api.go, redwood/uecon/cli.go - redwood-console/src/components/RecommendationCard.tsx - docs/ops/autotune.md - docs/console/uecon.md - tests/integration/autotune_e2e_test.go - CI: .github/workflows/uecon.yaml (integration canary job) Review thread (high level): - Jun Park (reviewer): 'Can we ensure controller respects tenant-level overrides and does not change configs for routes with explicit manual settings?' - Author (Maya): 'Yes — autotune is disabled for any route with manual overrides; added an extra unit test and telemetry flag `autotune.manual_override_skipped=true`.' - Sofia Martinez: 'Quant profiles look good; add a small note about expected quality delta and a link to the eval harness results.' - Author: 'Added quality_delta field and linked eval-harness artifact; updated docs with expected QC numbers and toggles.' - Ethan Li: 'Integration test flaked once on CI (race in metrics collector).' - Author: 'Fixed by adding a metrics wait and retry in the test; reran CI.' CI Summary: - unit tests: pass - integration (canary): pass on main canary and on dedicated canary region - lint: pass - docs link check: pass Release notes: "Introduces opt-in autotune defaults for batching and KV caching, a quantization profile registry with automatic selection heuristics, and a new unit-economics simulation tool available via CLI and Console. This feature is opt-in and safe by default. See docs/ops/autotune.md for migration steps." Rollout plan: - Feature flagged behind `cost_opt_autotune_v1`. - Canary enabled for 5% of new routes for 2 weeks. - Monitor token cost delta and error metrics; auto-roll back if SLO regressions > 1%. Migration notes: - Existing routes will not be changed unless explicitly marked `autotune: true`. - Admins can preview suggestions in Console and apply changes manually or via the CLI. Follow-ups/known limitations: - Quant profiles are initial v1 and will be extended with model-specific evals (ENG-4291). - The unit-econ simulation currently uses historical pricing and does not include committed-reservation pricing models; follow-up planned. Merge: Squash-merged by Jun Park after approvals from all reviewers.
